rationale: The redesign removes supplier emissions evidence and accredited verification as launch-critical dependencies by narrowing the paid offer to a treasury exposure register built from contractually defined importer records and public defaults; regulated verification remains outside scope. It replaces assumed referral-led SaaS distribution with direct prepaid implementations and makes recurring workflow access contractible through a proposed importer workflow-integration and data-processing agreement. Because no agreement, paid buyer, channel or unit economics is established, control status remains unknown and every economic range is explicitly a validation hypothesis. The route is nevertheless lawful and economically coherent enough to test because research supports a current regulated cash event, recurring work and access contractibility, while identifying no fatal illegality or unobtainable essential right.

structural_change.control_instrument: Unsigned proposed 12-month workflow-integration and data-processing agreement defining importer data extracts, quarterly treasury-register use, prepaid work orders, processing duties and for-cause termination; public-default diagnostic is the refusal fallback and creates no claimed present right.
structural_change.customer_relationship_owner: The prospective business would directly own importer service contracts and billing relationships; no customer contract is currently signed.
structural_change.dependency_change: Removes supplier-provided actual-emissions evidence and accredited verifier outputs as launch-critical inputs; replaces them with defined importer-provided records under a contractible agreement and public regulatory defaults, leaving importer adoption as the critical dependency.
structural_change.distribution_instrument: Direct importer service contract and billing relationship acquired through targeted outbound; optional nonexclusive written broker or adviser referral agreements are pursued only after direct acquisition economics are measured.
structural_change.fully_loaded_economic_effects: Shifts from a 70,000 PLN SaaS build and assumed 75-85% contribution margin to an estimated 45,000 PLN productized-service launch with prepaid setup and quarterly fees, 12-25 initial delivery hours, 3-8 quarterly hours, explicit analyst/support/security/legal costs and unvalidated 45-65% setup and 60-75% retainer contribution margins. It reduces working-capital exposure and excludes verifier and supplier-collection costs, but lowers scale and leaves CAC, renewal and price tolerance unknown.
structural_change.incumbent_response_defensibility: Low-priced specialists and SAP can copy, bundle or underprice forecasting. The only plausible defense is faster, ERP-neutral deployment and accumulated customer-specific variance workflow; it is not exclusive and must earn renewal through measured treasury use.
